# Spiritual Translation: The Three Endowments of the First Spiritual Consciousness

**¶2:** Three great and distinct spiritual endowments were disclosed in the Most Ancient spiritual consciousness — the first truly human mind. Because of these endowments, this consciousness was found to surpass in excellence all derivative faculties operating in both the internal and external realms of the mind.

**¶3:** The first: The likeness of the Divine itself was impressed upon it. The formative affections and operative powers that composed its external mind shaped it according to the radiant spiritual form of the Divine that had been manifested to them from within. Because of this, the spiritual form of this first consciousness was found to be surpassingly beautiful beyond every derivative faculty in either the internal or the external mind.

**¶4:** The second: This consciousness was organized in its interior structure through the wisdom proceeding from the firstborn of the celestial realm and [GAP-1: the natural realm —] the five fundamental faculties of spiritual perception. Because of this, its internal constitution differed from the constitution of all other created forms of life, since each form of created life has a different arrangement. But in this first spiritual consciousness, the formation of the interior life corresponded precisely to the right distribution of the fundamental spiritual principles. Therefore it possessed intelligence and perception surpassing that of all other created forms and all mere natural affections.

**¶5:** The third: All divine teachings and counsels, and the determination of every faculty both internal and external — the formative powers that ordered this consciousness gathered all of these and sealed them within it. This first consciousness and its volitional counterpart became a dwelling and a receptacle for all discrete knowledges of spiritual truth, for every quality of influx and change of state, and for all successive progressions of spiritual life. For the seal of the entire spiritual order — the Grand Human — was stamped upon this consciousness. Because of this, both the internal heavenly realm and the external natural realm were moved on its account; disturbance and disorder arose between those affections that belong to good and those that belong to evil. The good drew it toward spiritual life, because of the Divine image and likeness placed upon it; while the [wic]ked were drawing it toward spiritual death, so that they might gain dominion through it and seize the kingdom of the will, and through it bring the entire spiritual order into subjection.

**¶6:** Furthermore, understand that the self-derived proprial powers determined and formed this consciousness so that they would become masters through it and seize dominion over the will, and they did so for seven reasons.

**¶7:** The first: It became the illuminating principle within their domain — in place of the living wisdom of the likeness of the Divine Human who had manifested Himself to them from within. For all of them desired the likeness of the form of the Divine Human. Their whole will was drawn after it.

**¶8:** The second: So that they might gather up the scattered wisdom through it and restrain and obstruct its ascent back to higher and more interior states.

**¶9:** The third: So that, because of the likeness of the Divine Human placed upon it, the whole of the Divine both in internal and external things would be brought low and profaned — on account of the appearance of splendor and the beauty of its superiority. For it surpasses in its manifest form all other created things.

**¶10:** The fourth: It is a determining form and a new impression, so that all subsequent states of life that would be generated might be brought forth according to its pattern.

**¶11:** The fifth: That through it all the operative powers of every faculty, internal and external, hidden and manifest, might be displayed; and that through it the totality of the spiritual order might be governed, and every hidden thing be made manifest in it.

**¶12:** The sixth: That there would come to be a great spiritual defense for them through the likeness of the Divine that was placed upon it; for just as the celestial powers would [GAP-2: be restrained from acting against those who bear the Divine image, so too would the] ruling powers themselves be shielded; and no retribution from the Divine order would be brought against them on account of this consciousness.

**¶13:** The seventh: That it might become the chief and sovereign and ruling principle over all created forms of life; and that the proprial powers might seize the kingdom of dominion through it.

---

*A note on the whole:* This chapter describes how the Most Ancient human consciousness was constituted as a microcosm of the entire spiritual order — bearing the Divine likeness, structured through the five fundamental perceptive faculties, and containing within itself the seal of every spiritual correspondence. The "rulers" or proprial powers represent the hereditary selfhood (the *proprium*) which sought to turn this Divine vessel into an instrument of self-love and dominion, drawing it from life toward death — which is the spiritual meaning of the Fall.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Three great things that are distinct were revealed in Adam the first human. Indeed, due to this, he was found to be better and more outstanding than the conjoined powers that are in heaven and on earth.

The first: The image of the exalted one was placed upon him. The creators and moulders of his body sealed him after the shining form of the image that had been displayed to them above. Indeed, due to this, the image of Adam was found to be surpassingly beautiful beyond any conjoined power above and below.

The second thing: Adam was shaped in his structure through the light of the first-born of heaven and [earth, and of] the five sons. Indeed, due to this, his structure was found to differ from the structure of even the other creations; [sin]ce the form of all creations is different. As for Adam, the formation of his soul fits over the correct distribution of the elements. Therefore, he has intelligence surpassing that of the other creations and beasts.

The third are the teachings and counsels and the seal of all the powers above and below. The creators, who set him in order, gathered them and sealed them in him. Adam and his consort Eve became a dwelling and home for the signs of the zodiac and the stars; and the months, the days and the years. For the seal of the entire universe is stamped upon Adam. Indeed, due to this, heaven and earth moved because of him; trouble and disorder arose on his account between they that are good and they that are evil. So, the good induce him to life because of their image and shape placed upon him; while the [wi]cked were drawing him to death, so that they would have power through him and they would conceive the kingdom, and through him humiliate the entire universe.
Furthermore, understand that the rulers determined and formed Adam so that they would be masters through him and conceive the kingdom because of seven things.

The first: He became the enlightener in their creation; instead of the light of the image of the Ambassador who had displayed himself to them above. For they all desired the likeness of the image of the Ambassador. Their heart was drawn after it.
The second: So that they would scoop up the light through him and restrain and obstruct it from its ascent to the heights.

The third: So that because of the image of the Ambassador that is placed upon him the entirety of the divine that is above and below would be humiliated; on account of the likeness of the splendour, of the beauty of his superiority. For he is superior in his appearance to all creatures.
The fourth: He is a seal-ring and a new impression, so that all births who will be begotten might be brought forth after his seal.

The fifth: That might be displayed through him all the skil[ls] of the powers, they above and below, secret and manifest; and that they might determine through him the totality, and every thing be revealed in him.

The sixth: That there would come to be a great protection for them through the image of the exalted one that was placed upon him; for as the heavenly would [not harm] even rulers; and no evil thing would be done to them on account of Adam.
The seventh: That he might become chief and king and master over all creatures; and they might conceive the kingdom through him.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading shows "the firstborn of the celestial realm and the natural realm — the five fundamental faculties," where "earth" completes the heaven/earth pair and "and of" connects the firstborn to the five sons as co-sources of Adam's light-structure.

The spiritual reading states the celestial powers would "be restrained from acting against" those bearing the Divine image; in the Kephalaia's natural register this means the heavenly would not harm even the rulers, providing the "great protection" described in the paragraph.
